part.text:
All 10 tests pass. Here's what I implemented in `connect.py`:

## Solution

**`ConnectGame.__init__`** — parses the board string into a grid of tokens, stripping the decorative indentation from each line (the parallelogram shape is implied by the game's geometry, not the string).

**`get_winner`** — checks whether player `O` connects top→bottom, then whether player `X` connects left→right (a valid Hex game can have at most one winner); returns `""` if neither.

**`_connects(player, side)`** — a DFS flood fill from all of the player's stones on the starting edge, checking reachability of the opposite edge.

The key detail was the hex adjacency for the right-leaning parallelogram: since each row is shifted half a cell (one character) to the right, a cell at `(r, c)` is adjacent to:

- `(r, c-1)`, `(r, c+1)` — same row
- `(r-1, c)`, `(r-1, c+1)` — row above
- `(r+1, c-1)`, `(r+1, c)` — row below

This correctly rejects diagonal-only connections (the "illegal diagonal" test) while allowing the zig-zag paths the real Hex game permits.

No new files were created, and `connect_test.py` was left untouched.
